The evidence suggests that Neogitogenin acts as a target for Solute carrier family 22 member 7, which is a known target of Ochratoxin alpha. Additionally, Neogitogenin is also shown to target CAKI-2, which is a cell line that is a target of a complex compound, and this compound further targets A-431. These findings collectively suggest that Neogitogenin may interact with a series of molecular targets that ultimately lead to the inhibition of A-431. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential mechanism by which Neogitogenin could influence A-431, although the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
